content.thinking: Small grids with 128 rows already spread 640 CTAs across all 148 SMs at 4–5 per SM. Next I'll run the latency map (probe 2), measuring single-thread dependent loads cold from DRAM, warm after a same-SM touch, and warm after a different-SM touch.

I found that clock reads were scheduled before the load result was waited on, causing every reading to show 13 cycles. I'll fix this by storing the loaded value to shared memory and making the next address depend on it to force the wait.

The probe is working, showing warm L2 hits at 255–309 cycles vs. cold DRAM reads at 560–1100 cycles. Next I'll run the full map covering cold, self-warm, and cross-SM-warm cases, then analyze bimodality and address bits.

Latency is bimodal between dies (~585 vs 994 cycles cold, ~280 vs 657 warm), but the die split isn't simply `smid < 74` or any single address bit. I'll map the die of all 148 SMs, check how often the home flips between neighboring 128 B lines, and fit an XOR hash over GF(2).

Found that the home die within 1 MB is given by the XOR of VA bits 12-15, 17-19 (100% fit), with an uneven 70/78 SM split interleaved in TPC pairs. Next I'll verify whether this hash still holds across 2 MB pages over a 64 MB range, since that involves physical page bits.

Next I'll refit the in-page hash with bit 20 included and run the local-streaming bandwidth test—if that's not faster, the idea doesn't hold regardless of the hash.
